questions.q: A company keeps customer records in an Amazon RDS database and wants to find which columns contain PII using Amazon Macie. What should the data engineer do?

options.t: Point a Macie discovery job at the RDS instance
options.why: Wrong: Macie only reads Amazon S3 general purpose buckets.

options.t: Export or replicate the data to S3 (for example with DMS or Glue) and run a Macie job on the export
options.why: Right: Macie analyzes S3 only, so land the data in S3 first.

options.t: Enable Macie automated discovery in the RDS console
options.why: Wrong: automated discovery samples S3 buckets, not databases.

options.t: Enable Macie in the Region and wait for it to scan all data stores
options.why: Wrong: enabling Macie does not scan non-S3 stores.

questions.explain: Macie scans S3 only; other stores must be exported to S3 first.
questions.remember: Macie = S3 only. For RDS, DynamoDB or Redshift data, export or land it in S3 (DMS, Glue, UNLOAD), then scan the export.
variants: Data already in an S3 data lake → run a Macie job directly on the bucket.
The sensitive data is in scanned images → Macie does not OCR; use Textract plus Comprehend PII.

questions.q: After Macie finds PII in a data lake, analysts must see the data with the PII hidden. Which approach meets this?

options.t: Configure a Macie job to redact the PII in the objects
options.why: Wrong: Macie finds sensitive data but never changes it.

options.t: Use Glue Detect PII transforms or Lake Formation column and cell filters to mask or hide it
options.why: Right: masking companions act on the data, Macie only reports locations and counts.

options.t: Suppress the Macie findings with a suppression rule
options.why: Wrong: suppression only hides findings, the data stays exposed.

options.t: Add the PII values to a Macie allow list
options.why: Wrong: an allow list stops Macie reporting those matches, it does not protect the data.

questions.explain: Macie detects; masking is done by Glue, Lake Formation or Redshift masking.
questions.remember: Macie finds, it does not mask or redact. Pair it with Glue Detect PII, Lake Formation filters or Redshift dynamic data masking.
variants: Data sits in Redshift and must be masked for some users → Redshift dynamic data masking.
Only need to know where PII lives → Macie findings are enough.

questions.q: A company wants Macie to detect its internal customer IDs, which follow a fixed pattern and usually appear near the word 'CustID'. What should be configured?

options.t: A managed data identifier
options.why: Wrong: managed identifiers are built in and do not know company-specific formats.

options.t: A custom data identifier with a regex and keywords
options.why: Right: regex defines the pattern and keywords with a match distance reduce false positives.

options.t: An allow list with the ID pattern
options.why: Wrong: an allow list suppresses matches, the opposite of detecting them.

options.t: A suppression rule on the findings
options.why: Wrong: it hides findings and cannot create detections.

questions.explain: Company-specific formats need a custom data identifier (regex plus optional keywords).
questions.remember: Own format to detect → custom data identifier (regex, keywords, ignore words). Expected matches to ignore → allow list.
variants: Public company phone numbers keep being flagged → allow list.
Standard credit card numbers → a managed data identifier already covers them.

questions.q: A security team wants a bucket that becomes publicly accessible to be fixed within minutes, automatically. Macie already monitors the account. Which design fits?

options.t: Review the Macie console weekly and fix buckets by hand
options.why: Wrong: manual and slow.

options.t: Macie policy finding to an EventBridge rule that invokes a Lambda function to enable Block Public Access
options.why: Right: Macie publishes findings as EventBridge events in near real time, enabling auto-remediation.

options.t: Run a daily scheduled Macie job on all buckets
options.why: Wrong: jobs inspect object content and run on a schedule, so they are not near real time.

options.t: Enable Macie automated sensitive data discovery
options.why: Wrong: it scores sensitive content, it does not fix bucket access.

questions.explain: Policy finding to EventBridge to Lambda gives near-real-time remediation.
questions.remember: Findings are EventBridge events: route to Lambda, SNS, SQS or Step Functions for remediation or tickets.
variants: Findings must be kept for the long term and aggregated → send to Security Hub or S3.
Only a notification is needed → EventBridge rule to SNS.

questions.q: A Macie job reports access denied on objects encrypted with SSE-KMS using a customer managed key. The bucket policy is fine. What is the fix?

options.t: Allow the Macie service-linked role to use `kms:Decrypt` and `kms:DescribeKey` in the key policy
options.why: Right: Macie must decrypt objects to analyze them.

options.t: Switch the objects to client-side encryption
options.why: Wrong: Macie cannot analyze client-side encrypted objects.

options.t: Enable S3 Block Public Access on the bucket
options.why: Wrong: it is not related to Macie reading objects.

options.t: Lower the job sampling depth
options.why: Wrong: sampling depth does not grant permissions.

questions.explain: The customer managed key policy must allow Macie's service-linked role to decrypt.
questions.remember: Cannot read SSE-KMS objects → add the Macie service-linked role to the key policy. Also exempt it from SCPs or bucket Deny statements.
variants: An SCP or bucket Deny blocks non-listed roles → exempt the Macie service-linked role.
The results bucket key → must let Macie GenerateDataKey.

questions.q: A Macie job at 100% sampling over a very large lake produces an unexpectedly high bill. Which actions reduce cost? Choose TWO.

options.t: Lower the sampling depth for the first pass
options.why: Right: cost is per GB inspected, so sampling less inspects less.

options.t: Scope jobs with prefix and last-modified criteria and exclude log or public-data buckets
options.why: Right: fewer bytes inspected means lower cost.

options.t: Compress all objects to Parquet to shrink bytes
options.why: Wrong: compression expands during analysis, so it does not reduce the cost.

options.t: Enable Macie in every Region for balance
options.why: Wrong: unused Regions only add cost.

options.t: Run a full scan every day
options.why: Wrong: it repeats inspection; use incremental jobs on last-modified instead.

questions.explain: Macie cost is per GB inspected; sample and scope.
questions.remember: Reduce Macie cost by sampling, scoping to important buckets and prefixes, excluding low-value buckets and running incremental jobs.
variants: Need to know cost before running → use the cost estimate on job creation.
Job stops partway through the month → monthly analysis quota (5 TB default) was reached.

questions.q: A company with many accounts wants Macie jobs and findings managed centrally, and every new account covered automatically. What should it do?

options.t: Invite each account manually and enable Macie in each
options.why: Wrong: invitations do not auto-cover new accounts and scale worse.

options.t: Use Organizations with a delegated Macie administrator and auto-enable for new accounts
options.why: Right: the admin runs jobs and sees member findings; auto-enable covers new accounts.

options.t: Enable Macie in the management account only
options.why: Wrong: member accounts are not scanned.

options.t: Use GuardDuty S3 protection instead
options.why: Wrong: it detects suspicious access, not sensitive content.

questions.explain: Delegated administrator plus auto-enable via Organizations.
questions.remember: Multi-account Macie → Organizations delegated admin with auto-enable. Macie is per Region, so repeat per Region.
variants: Findings from many Regions in one place → Security Hub aggregation or EventBridge.
Detect suspicious access to S3 → GuardDuty.

questions.q: PDFs in an S3 bucket are scans of paper forms (images of text) and may contain PII. Macie finds nothing. What is the best way to detect the PII?

options.t: Increase Macie sampling depth to 100%
options.why: Wrong: Macie does not OCR images, so deeper sampling will not help.

options.t: Extract the text with Textract and detect PII with Comprehend
options.why: Right: Textract performs OCR and Comprehend finds PII in text.

options.t: Add a custom data identifier
options.why: Wrong: regex cannot match text that is not extracted from the image.

options.t: Convert the files to ZIP
options.why: Wrong: archives are extracted but images inside still are not read.

questions.explain: Macie has no OCR; use Textract plus Comprehend.
questions.remember: Images and scans → Textract (OCR) then Comprehend PII. Macie handles text-based files, documents, Parquet and archives.
variants: Text-based PDFs, CSV or Parquet → Macie can analyze them.
Files above Macie's size limits are skipped entirely.
